name: Additive public menu, serving offers, ordering, demand intelligence, and POS-lite architecture direction
phase: Architecture direction only; no implementation or activation authorized
foundation: FOOD-001A-K remains the private versioned draft/evidence/compliance foundation. FOOD-002 is additive and never replaces it.
canonicalDish: One stable FoodDishId identifies a customer-recognizable dish.
Versioned public dish presentations reference exact FOOD-001 product and recipe versions.
Do not duplicate a dish merely because it is offered at another serving scale.

servingOffers.model: Versioned commercially distinct serving offers beneath one dish; serving format describes style/scale, while the offer represents the eventual purchasable choice only after independent readiness and authorization.
rules: Unknown values remain explicitly unresolved, never guessed.
Do not infer family/catering servings by multiplying individual portions.
Future bundles reference component offers rather than disconnected duplicate dishes.

recordStatus: All FOOD-002 record families are proposed future additive concepts, not existing implemented records.
readinessRules: Draft existence, structural completeness or reviewed state never automatically publishes or enables ordering.
One reviewed serving format does not establish review or permission for every format.
Code and publication are not legal/safety/tax/payment/fulfillment approval; no cottage-food, catering or hot-food permission is assumed.
publicProjection: Public publication exposes only an explicit allowlisted projection.
Never automatically serialize private evidence, reviewer identities, internal operating addresses or entire private drafts.
An informational published page can exist with ordering disabled.

menuAuthority.model: Data-driven menu, not hard-coded pages; sections reference ordered dish/offer entries; featured state is explicit editorial configuration.
rules: One authoritative availability source eventually drives every surface.
Display/cache projections are never authoritative for accepting orders; revalidate before charging.
Availability updates propagate through projections rather than manual edits across pages.
Family ordering is first-class, not multiple individual meals.
Catering may initially remain inquiry-only.
Catering-compatible offers may show pan size, estimated servings, minimum, lead time, event notes and fulfillment restrictions.
Keep customer interaction simple despite richer operational rules.

cartAndQuotation: Persistent cart state is convenience only.
Server quotations revalidate exact offer versions, availability, price, tax treatment, discounts, fees and fulfillment.
Never silently substitute recipe, format, price or fulfillment option.
Confirmation-page navigation is not proof of payment.

orderLifecycle.separation: Operational state is separate from payment state. Cancellation, failure, rescheduling and refund flows are separately modeled.

fulfillment: Order initiated on site before fulfillment; local service.
Delivery/meetup/pickup only where reviewed and operationally supported.
Farther requests may require manual approval of fee/window before charge.
No shipping assumption and no hard-coded radius, fees, hours or address.

rules: A Google Voice-style number can fit the model, but no provider is selected.
Missing configuration hides capabilities; never fall back to private/personal data.
No real telephone, location, address, hours or business listing is assumed.

qrArchitecture.identity: Stable opaque public aliases, not private IDs or authorization-bearing tokens.
rules: Support packaging, labels, thank-you cards, first-order/reward cards and catering materials without generating assets now.
Separate current dish/reorder destinations from exact historical package information; old packages must not silently show changed recipe details.
QR supplements, never replaces, required physical/pre-payment disclosures.

reorder: Reconstruct a proposed cart from historical offers and revalidate current eligibility, availability, pricing and fulfillment.
Never auto-charge, guarantee old price/availability or silently substitute changed configuration.

feedback.separation: Private operational feedback is separate from optional public social proof.
feedback.verification: Prefer verified completed-order linkage and purchased serving format. Account creation is not required solely to verify order-linked feedback.
rules: Keep raw verified feedback so presentation can change later.
Insufficient evidence means no public rating claim. Public stars are never automatic.
Separate raw observations from derived metrics and client engagement from authoritative server order/payment events.
No addresses, contact information or feedback text in general analytics events.
Abandonment is derived rather than directly proven.
Sell-through needs actual inventory denominators; repeat-customer rates need defensible customer linkage.

publicLabels: You Asked, We Brought It Back
rules: Preserve unavailable periods, serving-format differences and seasonality/time/day-of-week context.
Recommendations are advisory; River retains final publishing/menu control.
Labels require documented evidence rules or explicitly editorial treatment; editorial treatment cannot fabricate factual demand/popularity/scarcity claims.
Never fabricate demand, scarcity, popularity, ratings or order counts. Limited Batch requires a real batch/capacity basis.
Authorized private workspace only; deposits/settlements are not additional sales.
No terminal hardware, cash drawers, payroll, employee scheduling or enterprise restaurant functionality.

customerIdentity: Browsing and first ordering do not require accounts; collect only transaction/fulfillment necessities.
Later customer identity supports history, favorites, saved preferences, reorder and rewards.
Public dish IDs, QR aliases and guessed order IDs never grant private authorization.
CRM linkage is explicit and consent-aware; ordering never automatically enrolls customers in marketing.
reuseCandidates: FOOD-001A-K: domain, immutable persistence, authorization, controller, transport and runtime capability patterns
src/lib/commerce/product-catalog.ts: canonical product and integer-cent pricing patterns, not digital checkout/delivery authority
src/lib/commerce/payment-event.ts and src/lib/commerce/d1-order-persistence.ts: verified event and durable replay patterns, requiring deliberate physical-order adaptation
River OS CRM consent/attribution patterns; shared identity/session foundations
Raw-versus-derived analytics patterns, without insurance domain authority
Existing reader/browser persistence patterns, not an existing food cart
reuseRules: Do not import digital-commerce checkout/delivery assumptions or insurance/Sesh authority into food.
Use shared content/media foundations with explicit approved media references; do not create a duplicate food media system.
Existing digital commerce does not establish physical-food ordering, provider support or legal readiness.
designDirection: fast dish-to-cart flow and minimal checkout steps when separately activated
tasteful persistent cart/Order Now capability gated by ordering activation
noInventedContent: No invented dishes, photography, prices, phone number, address, hours or launch details.
implementationSequence: FOOD-002B pure canonical dish + versioned serving-offer domain
Payment integration only after external readiness and explicit approval
QR/reorder, verified feedback and demand observations as separate slices
Derived recommendations and optional public social proof
futureScopeRule: Every persistence, route, configuration, activation, payment and public-exposure step requires separately bounded approval/scope; this direction authorizes none.

food002B.objective: Pure canonical dish and versioned serving-offer domain linked to exact FOOD-001 references; no publication, commerce registration or sale enablement.
specificationDecisions: initial format vocabulary and future custom/bundle extension boundaries
food002B.status: Sufficiently bounded for specification; exact type/validator/invariant decisions must be settled there before implementation.

additiveRelationship: Existing creator, insurance, Sesh, content, commerce and community trajectories remain intact; neither replaces the other. Community activation remains separately gated.
currentTaskBoundary: Create only this architecture-direction specification. Do not implement, stage, commit, create routes/UI/schema/migrations, configure payment/runtime infrastructure or deploy.
